mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism is not activated during a simultaneous surge in wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong commodity price inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases risk premia and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism is not activated during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when credit spreads are widening sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals improving labor market conditions that support corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable within ±0.1pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of accelerating wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal savings (RSAFS) falling below its 5-year average while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) rise above their 5-year average signals a shift from saving to spending, which amplifies demand and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism is not activated during periods of high uncertainty (VIX > 30).
